task_context.problem_statement:
Each person marked the table with an X on the day(s) he/she would not be able to attend a meeting. On which day can the most people attend a meeting?

\begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|}
\multicolumn{6}{c}{}\\\hline
&Mon&Tues&Wed&Thurs&Fri\\\hline
Anna&X&&X&&\\\hline
Bill&&X&&X&X\\\hline
Carl&X&X&&X&X\\\hline
\end{tabular}
task_context.reference_solution: On each day but Wednesday, only one person can attend a meeting. On Wednesday, two people can. Thus, the day on which the most people can attend a meeting is $\boxed{\text{Wednesday}}.$

If the X marks the days they *cannot* attend, how does that change how you look for the day when the *most* people can attend?

Exactly. Since we want the maximum number of attendees, we want the minimum number of people who are unavailable. Now that you have the right approach, how would you analyze the columns of the table?

Monday: 2 X's
Tuesday: 2 X's
Wednesday: 1 X
Thursday: 2 X's
Friday: 2 X's

Since Wednesday only has one person who can't make it, that means it's the day with the most people available. I'll go with Wednesday!

You've correctly applied the logic! You identified the meaning of the markers, counted the absences for each day, and compared them to find the minimum. That is the perfect way to solve this type of problem.
